routes.label: Classify by the numbers of faces of each color

question: Each face of a regular tetrahedron is painted either red, white, or blue. Two colorings are considered indistinguishable if two congruent tetrahedra with those colorings can be rotated so that their appearances are identical. How many distinguishable colorings are possible?
solution:
Rotations preserve the number of faces of each color, so classify colorings by those counts. We must also check whether the same counts can produce different arrangements.

For this check, place one face at the bottom. A \(120^\circ\) rotation about the line through the opposite vertex and the bottom face's center cycles the other three faces.

Four faces of one color: There are \(3\) choices of color, giving \(3\) colorings.

Three faces of one color and one of another: Choose the color used three times in \(3\) ways and the other color in \(2\) ways, giving \(3\cdot2=6\). Put the single differently colored face at the bottom; the other faces are identical, so its original position creates no additional coloring.

Two faces of each of two colors: There are \(3\) choices of the unused color. To check uniqueness, put a face of one used color at the bottom. Among the other three faces, exactly one matches the bottom. The \(120^\circ\) turns move that matching face to any of the three positions, so there is only one arrangement for each chosen color pair. This gives \(3\) colorings.

Two faces of one color and one face of each remaining color: Choose the repeated color in \(3\) ways. Put a face of one specified singleton color at the bottom. The other singleton can occupy any upper position, and the \(120^\circ\) turns carry these positions into one another. Thus each repeated-color choice gives one coloring, for \(3\) more.

These are all ways to distribute four faces among at most three colors. The rotation arguments show uniqueness within each counted choice, while different color counts cannot become identical under rotation. Therefore the total is
\[
3+6+3+3=15,
\]
choice A.
